title: Substitution, not redesign
subtitle: The applied pesticide mixture in the median US county concentrated from 9.0 to 4.8 effective compounds as glyphosate took a third of all applied mass. The one federal indicator of agroecosystem redesign — cover crops — reached 4.7% of cropland.

y.label: Effective number of compounds (inverse Simpson), median county
y.note: The number of equally-used pesticides that would produce the observed concentration of applied mass. Insensitive to rare compounds, so a growing compound roster cannot produce the decline.

series.label: Effective number of compounds, median county
Cover crops, % of cropland (Census of Agriculture)
series.note: Only three observations exist; draw the points prominently and the connecting line as a dashed segment so the sparse sampling is visible.

annotations.text: 1992: 8 compounds make up half of all applied mass
The median county still applies ~89–125 different compounds. Richness held; the mass concentrated.
Cover crops: 2.64% → 4.70% of cropland in a decade (+74.9% of acreage). At the realised rate, half of US cropland in ~225 years.
2015: USGS stops estimating seed-treatment applications — the insecticide series breaks here, the glyphosate and diversity series do not.

Between-state association only: no-till share of cropland vs glyphosate share of applied mass, ρ = +0.62 (2012), +0.56 (2017), p < 0.0001 — a regional co-occurrence, not a farm-level effect. Cover-crop expansion 2012→2017 vs change in chemical diversity: ρ = +0.12, p = 0.42.

source_note: USGS Pesticide National Synthesis Project, county pesticide use 1992–2018 (EPest-high), corrected: California removed from every year and the double-counted METOLACHLOR & METOLACHLOR-S / DIMETHENAMID & DIMETHENAMID-P aggregate rows dropped. USDA Census of Agriculture 2012, 2017, 2022. Association only — the two sources are different sampling frames.

one_claim: For 26 years the US agricultural pesticide record shows input substitution — flat mass, a mixture concentrating onto one compound and one function — and no visible redesign phase.
